name: Goal-heading write (menotaxis)
mechanism: Write a bump at target heading in FC2 goal layer; PFL3 compares to EPG heading and nulls the error. PROVEN IN VIVO: focal optogenetic activation of FC2 makes flies orient along experimenter-defined directions while walking forward — the exact BCI lever, demonstrated.
bci_realism: High — 1-D variable, small target population, matches natural menotaxis
in_vivo_precedent: YES — FC2 optogenetics steers flies to arbitrary set direction (Mussells Pires 2024)

name: Direct steering command (PFL3 L/R)
model_hook: asymmetric ext to PFL3 L vs R
citation: Rayshubskiy et al. 2020 bioRxiv; Hulse et al. 2021 eLife
mechanism: PFL3 L-R activity difference drives DNa02 descending neurons -> contralateral turning. Bypasses goal comparison; imposes turn directly.
bci_realism: High — direct motor lever, fast, but open-loop (no heading memory)
in_vivo_precedent: YES — PFL3 optogenetic bias turns; DNa02 drives turning (Rayshubskiy 2020)

name: Compass gain / offset recalibration
model_hook: shift w_shift or inject ER offset
citation: Kim, Hermundstad et al. 2019 Nat Neurosci; Fisher et al. 2019 Nature
mechanism: Alter EPG-visual mapping so the fly's internal heading is offset from true heading -> systematic course bias.
bci_realism: Medium — slow, indirect, but persistent; good for standing bias
in_vivo_precedent: Partial — EPG remapping shown; behavioral bias inferred

name: Forward-speed drive
citation: Lu et al. 2022 Nature (PFN vector); Bidaye et al. 2020 Neuron
mechanism: PFN neurons encode traveling-direction vector amplitude; PFL2 modulates forward drive. Sets how fast the fly runs along its heading.
bci_realism: Medium — needed for point-to-point, separable from steering
in_vivo_precedent: Partial — PFN vector & PFL2 speed roles shown physiologically

name: Stop / pause
citation: Bidaye et al. 2020 Neuron; Cande et al. 2018 eLife
mechanism: DNp09 activation freezes locomotion. A discrete brake for arriving at a target / holding a formation slot.
bci_realism: High — single descending neuron, strong discrete effect

name: Reverse / backward walking
citation: Bidaye et al. 2014 Science; Feng et al. 2020
mechanism: MDN drives backward walking. Extends reachable maneuvers; less relevant to flight but key for walking swarms.
bci_realism: High for walking flies — single command line
in_vivo_precedent: YES — MDN drives backward walking (Bidaye 2014 Science)
